Here is a 5-paragraph summary of the news article:

***

The former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed by the Australian government to examine whether the country's laws adequately protect the human right to religious freedom. This move is designed to address the debate around religious amendments in a same-sex marriage bill, although the treasurer has stated that the review is "no substitute" for those amendments.

The prime minister, Malcolm Turnbull, has emphasized the importance of carefully examining the issue of religious freedom in light of the recent "yes" vote on marriage equality and the impending legislation. Some senior conservatives have suggested considering a separate religious freedom bill next year, while others insist it should be addressed alongside the marriage bill.

Ruddock has been asked to report his findings by March 31st. Turnbull has acknowledged that various proposals for legislative changes to protect freedom of religion have been put forward, but he cautions that such reforms should be undertaken carefully to prevent unintended consequences, especially from broadly worded "bill of rights-style declarations."

The government is particularly concerned about the uncertainties that could arise from such legislative changes. Turnbull has stated that Ruddock's review will serve as a "timely expert stocktake" to inform the consideration of any necessary reforms to protect religious freedom.

Turnbull believes that Ruddock, who has served as Australia's special envoy for human rights, is the right person to conduct this review and provide the government with the necessary guidance on this sensitive and complex issue.
